runs.text:
Some truths need no argument. All men are equal, and their Creator gives them rights no one may take away: among them, life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. Governments exist to secure these rights, and get their power only from the consent of the governed. When a government works against these ends, the people may change it or scrap it, and build a new one on whatever principles seem likeliest to bring them safety and happiness.

Long-established governments should not be swapped for light cause, and history bears this out: people put up with evils rather than right themselves by scrapping familiar forms. But when a long train of abuses, all pointing to the same end, betrays a design to reduce them to absolute despotism, they have both the right and the duty to throw off such a government and find new guards for their future security.

Prudence, indeed, will dictate that Governments long established should not be changed for light and transient causes; and accordingly all experience hath shewn, that mankind are more disposed to suffer, while evils are sufferable, than to right themselves by abolishing the forms to which they are accustomed. But when a long train of abuses and usurpations, pursuing invariably the same Object evinces a design to reduce them under absolute Despotism, it is their right, it is their duty, to throw off such Government, and to provide new Guards for their future security.
